ai.description: Trachischium fuscum reaches 30–40 cm. It is uniform dark brown or black above with a distinctively bright yellow or orange belly. The head is indistinct from the neck, and scales are smooth and glossy.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trachischium fuscum* is best distinguished by its uniform, dark-pigmented belly, which contrasts with the pale or checkered ventral patterns found in other *Trachischium* species.
ai.habitat: *Trachischium fuscum* inhabits moist, high-altitude temperate forests and alpine meadows in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Blackbelly Worm-eating Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through damp soil in search of earthworms and other soft prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trachischium fuscum* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, though specific reproductive data remains limited.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trachischium fuscum* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
